headline: Running has stayed away long enough that the trail block is now fully behind you. One lift last week, but no strength rhythm and no top-end reading in weeks. The base is enormous — the loading side has simply gone quiet.
confidence_reasons: No recent activity data in last 3 days

sections.overview: The picture right now is a large, intact endurance base sitting under a genuinely quiet loading period. The recent trail block was massive — the four-week running total dwarfs the prior block — and everything since has been recovery from that, not fresh work. Strength touched down once but hasn't strung together a cadence, so neither of the two main load channels is currently contributing. What's holding the floor up is background movement: step counts stay high even on rest days, which keeps you from being truly sedentary but does nothing for either aerobic or neuromuscular development. The strain-versus-tolerance reading flagging "detraining" is simply the arithmetic catching up to a real absence of tracked sessions — not a surprise given the data, but worth naming as confirmation rather than alarm. Sleep has been thin and inconsistent lately, which is context for why the pause might feel earned even if nothing in the training log demands it.
sections.trends: The year-to-date shape is strongly positive — you're carrying roughly four times last year's distance to the same date, which tells you the annual arc is building, not stalling. The 16-week view shows a big trail-block spike followed by this deliberate trough, which is a normal cyclical shape after a concentrated durability effort. That shape makes sense for a hybrid athlete who maintains year-round readiness rather than periodising to one event. What's now stretching the interpretation is duration: the trough has run long enough that it's no longer a reset and is functioning as a genuine off-stretch. That's a choice, not a problem — but the longer it runs, the more the next few sessions become the real data point rather than the base behind them.
sections.threshold: Threshold pace and the VO2 picture are unchanged simply because there's been no qualifying data to move them — the last threshold reading is from early July and nothing recent has tested that end. Everything logged in the trail block sat deep in Z1 at very easy paces, which builds durability but tells you nothing about where your threshold currently is. So the honest read is that your aerobic ceiling is undemonstrated right now, not declined. A single tempo or faster effort would resolve that uncertainty quickly — until then, treat the current number as a stale but probably-still-valid estimate.
sections.zones: The recent block was almost entirely Z1 — heavily skewed toward the bottom, which is exactly right for high-volume time-on-feet trail work and shows no grey-zone creep at all. The per-session shapes confirm genuinely easy efforts: caps well controlled, only brief incidental touches higher on the longer days. That distribution served the trail block's intent cleanly. What the block-level picture is now missing entirely is any upper-zone stimulus — the top end has been dormant for an unusually long stretch, and the intensity distribution has become one-dimensional purely by absence rather than design.
sections.hr_comparison: Nothing concerning in the strength HR patterns — the lifting sessions that carry HR sit sensibly in the low-to-mid range for functional work, with occasional higher-tempo blocks visible in the older sessions. The most recent lift carries no HR at all, so there's less to read there. Source agreement across run and strength data looks consistent and directionally sound; no divergence worth flagging.
sections.calendar: The calendar tells the clearest story: a dense cluster of running through mid-August, then a clean stop, with only a single strength touch since. The running streak has reset to zero from a long prior run, which underlines that this is a real break in cadence rather than a light week. The one lift breaks the silence but doesn't establish a pattern. Consistency has been the athlete's hallmark, so the interpretation hinges on whether this quiet stretch is a chosen pause you'll close deliberately or one that's drifting.
sections.personal_bests: None of the speed PBs are in reach right now — they're all from a sharper, faster-paced period last year, and nothing in the current data touches those speeds. The ultra/50K mark reflects the durability side you've been feeding, and the base under you is more than deep enough to support that end. But PBs at either extreme need a return to actual structured work first; there's nothing actionable here until the loading resumes.

watch_items: Watch whether the first run back lands at a normal easy HR, confirming the trail block absorbed cleanly rather than left residual fatigue.
Watch whether running re-enters at all this week, or whether the off-stretch continues drifting from deliberate toward unplanned.
Watch for the first upper-zone or faster effort — the top end is now the single biggest blind spot in the data and needs a fresh reading.
